stem: Meher divides the positive length $12$ by a positive divisor. She wants to know whether the quotient is greater or less than $12$ from the size of the divisor alone.

parts.text: Which claim correctly predicts the quotient compared with $12$?

options.text: If the divisor is $4$, the quotient is less than $12$; if the divisor is $\dfrac{1}{2}$, the quotient is greater than $12$.
Every positive divisor makes the quotient less than $12$.
Every positive divisor makes the quotient greater than $12$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Dividing by a number greater than 1 shrinks the value ($12\div4=3$), while dividing by a number between 0 and 1 enlarges it ($12\div\frac{1}{2}=24$).

teacher.key_rationale: For positive quantities, divisor > 1 yields quotient < dividend; divisor between 0 and 1 yields quotient > dividend. Claiming one direction for every divisor misses that split.
